source: Rodríguez-Cuadrado, S., Valence, arousal, concreteness, familiarity and iconicity norms for 1,604 English words by Spanish L2 speakers of English, OSF project https://osf.io/rnbs5 (files posted 2026-07-23/24; no licence stated); and Scott, G. G., Keitel, A., Becirspahic, M., Yao, B. & Sereno, S. C. (2019), The Glasgow Norms: Ratings of 5,500 words on nine scales, Behavior Research Methods 51(3), 1258-1270, https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-018-1099-3 (open access, CC BY 4.0; PMC6538586)
rights: The OSF files state no licence: not committed; per-word means for the 72 words used are reproduced in people.json as derived values (quotation scale, attributed). The Glasgow Norms supplementary file is CC BY 4.0 with its article; only the 72 words' familiarity means are reproduced, attributed.

files.name: db.xlsx
files.osf_name: Database prevalence, valence, arousal, familiarity and concreteness in L2.xlsx
files.what: per-word L2 means; sheet Familiarity gives mean_familiarity over the raters who knew the word

files.name: raw.xlsx
files.what: trial-level ratings of 300 participants (id_variable 4 = familiarity, 1-7, 0 = don't know the word)
files.why: to re-compute and assert the 72 means and their rater counts

files.name: readme.docx
files.what: coding of id_variable and the scales

files.name: g2.csv
files.what: Glasgow Norms, 5,553 words, column FAM M (1-7), native English speakers from the University of Glasgow community
files.why: the second public: native readers, used to choose the words and to locate the family's order
